name: glkterm
why: A terminal implementation of the Glk interactive fiction API, a niche door into text adventure infrastructure.

brief.what_it_is: GlkTerm is a C library that implements the Glk interactive fiction API for a terminal window. It uses the curses.h screen control library to draw text windows and accept keyboard input, so Glk-based interpreters and games can run in a Unix terminal. The homepage is the Glk specification page, and GlkTerm appears there as one entry in a list of Glk libraries. The IF Archive lists it as glkterm-104.tar.gz, source for Glk 0.7.4, version 1.0.4, by Andrew Plotkin. A separate wide-character variant, glktermw-104.tar.gz, by Alexander Beels, uses ncursesw to display Unicode.
brief.why_it_exists: Glk is a standard interface that lets interactive fiction programs run on any platform that has a Glk library, so one game can work on many systems. GlkTerm supplies the terminal version of that interface.
brief.how_it_works: A Glk program calls the Glk API for windows, text input and output, and events. GlkTerm implements those calls on top of curses, which handles the terminal screen and keyboard. The homepage describes its scope only briefly and does not explain the internals.
brief.install_notes: No shell commands appear in the homepage or the IF Archive listing, so the install steps are not documented there. The homepage says GlkTerm is C source code that should compile on any Unix system or reasonable facsimile, provided curses.h is available. The wide-char build needs ncursesw or ncurses. Obtaining it means downloading the source tarball from the IF Archive and compiling it yourself. The Homebrew formula here is a library with no executables, so a Glk game or interpreter must be linked against it or run with a Glk-based interpreter.
brief.standout: Glk is a single API that many interpreters target, so GlkTerm lets the same interactive fiction runtime run in a plain terminal without a graphical toolkit. Its own author calls the library minimal and cheap, and the wider Glk family includes CheapGlk, which needs only stdio.h.
brief.status: Quiet or abandoned. The homepage says GlkTerm 1.0.4 is "No longer supported." The IF Archive shows glkterm-104.tar.gz and glktermw-104.tar.gz both last dated 14-Oct-2012. The homepage itself was last updated June 2, 2025, but that date refers to the Glk specification page, not to GlkTerm.
brief.caveats: The homepage explicitly says GlkTerm is no longer supported. It targets Glk 0.7.4, while the current spec is 0.7.6, so newer Glk features may be missing. It depends on curses or ncurses and is aimed at Unix-like systems. The Unicode variant is also unsupported and comes from a third-party modification. The homepage is a spec page rather than a GlkTerm project page, so there is no README, changelog, or usage guide to check against.
quotes: GlkTerm library 1.0.4 (C source code for a terminal-window Glk library, implemented using the curses.h screen control library.
Should compile on any Unix system or reasonable facsimile, as long as it has the curses.h library. (No longer supported.))
